text.p: STOCKS GOLD
Dow Jones close Latest spot rate
FTSE-100 close CRUDE OIL
Nikkei-225 latest $22.90 per bbl
U.S. stocks edged higher on Friday but bond prices fell as investors took profits after a four-day rally sparked by the Federal Reserve's decision on Tuesday to hold interest rates steady.
The dollar rose as investors continued to sell German marks amid improving prospects for a single European currency.
Gasoline prices shot up on lingering concerns about supplies of crude oil and refined products going into winter.

"We had a tidal wave of IPOs. But this market seems to be in a long pause. There's a lack of conviction and we have a good deal more economic reports next week," said Marty Kearney, a trader at PTI Securities.

The Dow Jones industrial average rose 4.07 to 5,872.92. For the week, the Dow fell 15.54 points. In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,291 to 1,010 on heavy volume of 407 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Kearney said the Dow has climbed more than 4 percent so far in September, not bad for what is historically the weakest month of the year.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 2.07 to 1,230.05, drawing nearer to June 5's record high of 1,249.15. The index was up 10.36 on the week.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond lost a quarter point to yield 6.91 percent, up from 6.88 percent on Thursday.

Wall Street next week faces a slew of economic reports, including the National Association of Purchasing Management index for September, August new home sales and leading indicators and Friday's key September employment data.

"Stocks are straggling on fears of a slowdown in the fourth quarter. But as in the past there's the usual difficulty for the market in reaching the next plateau, in this case 6,000" for the Dow, said Peggy Farley, chief executive officer of Amas Securities.

"We had a full calendar of IPOs this week with the last part of the week not showing as good a performance as they should have," she said. "The euphoria the (IPO) market saw in the spring has dissipated, there's less confidence."

As for the overall market, "the action has been quite good. It was a very volatile week and a lot of that volatility has been constructive in helping to arrest excesses," said Eugene Peroni, chief technical analyst with Janney, Montgomery Scott.
The dollar late Friday rose to 1.5244 marks from 1.5236 late Thursday and to 110.90 Japanese yen from 110.67.
Gasoline for October delivery settled up 1.61 cents to 64.60 cents a gallon on the New York Mercantile Exchange.
October heating oil ended up 0.59 cent to 71.49 cents a gallon after falling as low as 69.95 cents as traders took profits from this week's gains, which pushed the market to five-year highs.
Heating oil prices have risen more than 25 percent in the last three months as weekly data on stocks showed supplies well below those of a year ago and little buildup of stocks.
November crude ended 44 cents higher at $24.60 a barrel.

Overseas, London's FTSE 100 index added 13.2 points to close at 3,946.4, but was down 17.7 for the week. In Tokyo, The key 225-share Nikkei average rose 85.65 points to close at 21,547.02, which was up 434.78 from a week ago.
